issue.title: Shrink live-vault bob stats compute toward the 300 ms target
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-6l.6 (note #4) and bob-cli-6l.3 (note #2); first raised as DISCOVERED ISSUE note #1 on epic bob-cli-6l by bob-cli-6l.2.1.land.

Release `bob stats` on apollo's live vault (~/bob) measures 340–370 ms (overview 340 ms; -f json 370 ms; show worked -c 360 ms; metrics 340 ms; csv 360 ms; engine 7-day compute parity test 371 ms). The bob-cli-6l.land agent re-measured 0.34 s for `bob stats` at master f11ca41 on 2026-10-11. The Daily Stats plan (plan:202610/daily_stats.md, "Engine architecture") targeted <= 300 ms for the single-pass index (src/native/stats/index.rs) with parallel reads and no Tasks DSL. docs/stats.md#performance records 370 ms as the current budget and notes CLI wall time is within ~20 ms of the engine pass, so the cost is the index read itself.

Suggested approach: profile the index pass (file walk, per-file Tasks parse, done/ archive residence mapping, daily-note ledger/field scan) with a release build and `BOB_STATS_REAL_VAULT_PARITY=1 BOB_NOW='2026-10-11 12:00:00' cargo test --release --lib real_vault_parity_is_opt_in`; cut avoidable work (e.g. prefilter lines before the Tasks parser, skip ledger scans on non-daily notes); update the recorded numbers in docs/stats.md#performance. No timing assertions in CI.

task_type_fields.proposal: Profile and shrink the single-pass Daily Stats index so release bob stats on the live vault meets the original <=300 ms target, then update docs/stats.md#performance.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The Daily Stats plan made 300 ms a target with the measured number recorded and no CI timing assertions; the epic met that by recording 340–370 ms, so optimization is a separate pass rather than unfinished epic work.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-6l shipped bob stats at 340–370 ms on the live vault versus the plan's <=300 ms target; the epic recorded and re-budgeted the number, leaving optimization as a distinct pass.

payload.description: Both measure live-vault Tasks parsing cost; a shared parser speedup could serve both
Both concern the cost of bob stats runs; 6n speeds up each run, while this bug cuts redundant runs from the plugin

payload.entry: MacBook timing (Apple M1, bob 0.3.1, live vault, 2026-10-24, read-only over Tailscale SSH): bob stats show -a -f json -r 4w ran 310 ms on the first run, then 190-200 ms; a 5-metric 8-day explicit range ran 180-190 ms. Obsidian renders on that machine, so it already meets the 300 ms target. The 340-370 ms numbers come from apollo/athena; apollo under load (average 11-13) measures 0.4-0.6 s. Source: research:202610/daily_note_day_strip/daily_note_day_strip__final.md F3.

payload.entry: Measured sequential vs retained parallel-parse + shared session-scan on Athena and Apollo against read-only ~/bob with BOB_NOW='2026-10-11 12:00:00' and NO_COLOR=1. Sequential Apollo index medians were 395.10 ms (overview) and 432.04 ms (bob stats show -a -f json -r 4w): CPU-heavy Tasks 169.83–179.00 ms and daily 107.28–119.26 ms, not irreducible I/O (reads 41.44–49.14 ms). Shared per-note scan reuse did not move Apollo on its own; order-preserving parallel per-file parse is the measured win. Final warm index medians: Athena 56.35 / 59.65 ms, Apollo 169.40 / 187.09 ms. Both hosts meet the ≤300 ms index target. Apollo all-metrics wall ~334 ms is remaining compute outside the index. JSON baseline/final/baseline hashes were byte-identical (overview 246785 950b733fbb9de4894e407671d6a8f4c4ea4d13ec7257d26e11b450a840ec41bd; worked 161011 3b9ad19d62a7064bd1ab0dd5ef5b7398a28ee542a5b02cdbdb7c576cea095c72; all-metrics-4w 332396 d19e07796808709d25ad998f35887f7af7b8586cd933bdbdbe56245b7f9efce3; fixture 119672 43132814e3f399e9eb266a31ac4927de05f982dd94b16b208db3a3e233467ae5). Temporary Instant counters were removed before checks. Documented in docs/stats.md#performance. Release opt-in parity: compute 101 ms, CLI worked 112 ms. just check ToolRun 2d14035ae59696c70df69dc0789392cf succeeded in 231283 ms.

payload.close_reason: Apollo and Athena indexes are under 300 ms after parallel parse, with byte-identical JSON parity.
